entries.title: Florida's Missile Coast Takes Aim at the Space Age
entries.summary: 1960 — A U.S. Air Force Mace guided missile launch captured Florida's transformation from Atlantic coastline to missile range and Space Coast.

entries.title: The Hurricane That Helped Decide Who Would Control Florida
entries.summary: 1565 — A hurricane scattered Jean Ribault's French fleet as Spain and France struggled for control of Florida.

entries.title: Washington Takes Another Look at the St. Lucie River
entries.summary: 1941 — A federal engineering report on the St. Lucie River reached Congress as Florida's engineered waterway system continued to evolve.

entries.title: Miami Seaquarium Opens on Biscayne Bay
entries.summary: 1955 — Miami Seaquarium opened on Virginia Key, becoming part of South Florida's pre-Disney tourism landscape.

entries.title: A Photographer Records Miami After the Great Hurricane
entries.summary: 1926 — William A. Fishbaugh photographed Miami's destruction one week after the Great Miami Hurricane.

entries.title: Former Enemies Meet in Marianna to Return a Civil War Battle Flag
entries.summary: 1927 — Veterans and representatives from former enemies gathered in Marianna around a Confederate battle flag returned from Ohio.

entries.title: The Civil War Comes to Marianna
entries.summary: 1864 — Union troops under Alexander Asboth fought local Confederate defenders in the streets of Marianna.

entries.title: The Swamp Land Act Reshapes Florida's Future
entries.summary: 1850 — Congress transferred qualifying swamp and overflowed lands to the states, giving Florida a vast land base for reclamation and development.

entries.title: The 1896 Hurricane Devastates Cedar Keys
entries.summary: 1896 — A fast-moving hurricane drove a deadly storm surge across Cedar Key and Florida's Big Bend coast.

entries.title: Spain's Rum Ban Reaches Colonial Florida
entries.summary: 1714 — A royal order against cane liquor began a long journey through the Spanish Empire to colonial St. Augustine.

entries.title: Walt Disney World Opens in Central Florida
entries.summary: 1971 — The Magic Kingdom welcomed its first public guests and began reshaping Central Florida's economy, landscape and identity.

entries.title: Construction Begins on Castillo de San Marcos
entries.summary: 1672 — Spanish officials broke ground for the coquina fortress that still guards the St. Augustine waterfront.

entries.title: Union Forces Take St. Johns Bluff
entries.link_title: The Capture of St. Johns Bluff
entries.summary: 1862 — A combined Army-Navy operation outmaneuvered Confederate defenses guarding the St. Johns River.

entries.title: Sputnik Changes Cape Canaveral's Future
entries.summary: 1957 — The world's first artificial satellite accelerated the space race and made Florida's launch coast central to America's response.

entries.title: Madison Starke Perry Takes Office as Florida Approaches a Crossroads
entries.link_title: Madison Starke Perry Takes Office as Florida Approaches a Crossroads
entries.summary: 1857 — Florida's fourth governor began a term that combined railroad development and a boundary settlement with preparations for secession.

entries.title: Florida Asks Which Thanksgiving Belongs on the Calendar
entries.link_title: Florida Asks Which Thanksgiving Belongs on the Calendar
entries.summary: 1939 — An attorney general's letter to Governor Fred P. Cone exposed the confusion caused by competing Thanksgiving dates.

entries.title: A Royal Proclamation Creates East and West Florida
entries.link_title: A Royal Proclamation Creates East and West Florida
entries.summary: 1763 — Britain's October 7 proclamation divided its newly acquired Florida territory into two colonial governments.

entries.title: Mary Lee Graham Opens a Door in Key West's Business Leadership
entries.link_title: Mary Lee Graham Opens a Door in Key West's Business Leadership
entries.summary: 1953 — Mary Lee Graham became the first woman elected president of the Key West Chamber of Commerce.

entries.title: A Night Attack Brings War to Santa Rosa Island
entries.link_title: A Night Attack Brings War to Santa Rosa Island
entries.summary: 1861 — Confederate troops attacked a Union camp near Fort Pickens, but the battle did not dislodge the federal garrison.

entries.title: Hurricane Michael Changes the Florida Panhandle
entries.link_title: Hurricane Michael Changes the Florida Panhandle
entries.summary: 2018 — Michael made a catastrophic landfall near Mexico Beach and Tyndall Air Force Base; later analysis classified it as Category 5.

entries.title: The Great Hurricane of 1846 Destroys Key West's Lighthouses
entries.link_title: The Great Hurricane of 1846 Destroys Key West's Lighthouses
entries.summary: 1846 — A powerful hurricane wrecked Key West and Sand Key's lights, leaving a lasting story of loss and rebuilding.
